messages.subject: INLA survival model formulation using inla.stack and multiple likelihoods
parts:
Hi! I'm attempting to formulate a survival model jointly with a measurement error + exposure model (as in Muff et. al (2015) (https://www.jstor.org/stable/24771892) and more specifically Skarstein et. al (2023), example 4.3 (https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/bimj.202300078)), but I would like to do this using inla.stacks. So it is a Weibull survival model with a measurement error model for one covariate, and that introduces two additional levels to the model. I have formulated the model successfully by specifying the matrices manually (this can be found here: https://emmaskarstein.github.io/Missing-data-and-measurement-error/missing_and_mismeasured_covariate.html#me-model-ignoring-missing-observations) So I feel like it should not be a problem using inla.stacks to structure the data instead, but I'm struggling with the structure of the survival response.

One option, following this example: https://becarioprecario.bitbucket.io/spde-gitbook/ch-risk.html, would be to specify the time and event for inla.surv as separate vectors to the stack, and then call inla.surv directly in the formula. However, since I also need to include the responses for the measurement error model and exposure model in the formula, that won't work.

The other approach, more closely following my previous implementation using the matrices directly, would involve passing the inla.surv object as one list element to the stack data, together with two columns of NAs, and naming the list of all three of these Y. Then the formula could just have Y on the left hand side. However, when passing the inla.surv-object as one of the elements in a list as the data input in inla.stack, I get the error "Error in as.data.frame.default(x[[i]], optional = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = stringsAsFactors) : cannot coerce class ‘"inla.surv"’ to a data.frame".

I noticed the documentation for inla.stack says that the data argument should be a dataframe or a list of vectors, so I'm wondering if it is at all possible to structure the data for a survival model like this using stacks?

Here is some code to illustrate the issue (I've attached the whole code that continues this example in an R-file for further context):

# Exploring survival stacks

library(INLA)

n <- 100

t <- runif(n, 0, 10) # Survival time
d <- sample(c(0,1), n, replace = TRUE) # Survival event

x <- rnorm(n, 0, 1) # Covariate with measurement error
z <- rnorm(n, 0, 1) # Covariate without measurement error

data <- data.frame(t, d, x, z)

# Regression model of interest
# eta = beta.0 + beta.x*x + beta.z*z
Y.surv <- inla.surv(data$t, data$d)

stk_moi <- inla.stack(
    data = list(Y = list(Y.surv, rep(NA, n), rep(NA, n))), # THIS FAILS
    A = list(1),
    effects = list(
      list(beta.0 = rep(1, n),
           beta.x = 1:n,
           beta.z = data$z)),
    tag = "moi")

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA survival model formulation using inla.stack and multiple likelihoods
parts:
Hi Emma,

currently, you will have to use inla.stack() to construct the data
that will be used as the _input_ to inla.surv(), i.e. first call
inla.stack() to setup all the input data, and then call any special
observation object constructors afterwards (e.g. directly in the
formula) using inla.stack.data(...), collecting them into a list in
the case of multiple observation families., like
list(data.frame(y=y), inla.surv(...)) ~ ...

We have started working on the needed internal code restructuring for
allowing each observation model to be built separately and only _then_
combined into a joint model; once this is done that will also allow
inla.surv() to be used in the inlabru interface (that _always_
constructs each observation model separately and combines them
afterwards), meaning that there would be no more need for the user to
call inla.stack() themselves (models with special observation
objects/functions is the only remaining use case for user-code
inla.stack() calls); if that step will be needed at all, it will be
done internally by inlabru, like it currently does with all other
models.

Finn

parts:
Hi Finn, thank you for the reply!

I wasn't aware that I could specify a list of responses in the formula (though I guess that is in a way what I have already been doing by specifying just Y as the response), and I think that actually solves it quite nicely for me in this case.

Thank you also for the other information, I am working on a small R package for these kinds of measurement error models, and I'm using stacks to structure the data, which is how this became an issue for me. I have been considering basing it around inlabru, but since I'm more familiar with plain INLA I decided on using the stacks instead. But I may consider changing this in the future.

Best,
Emma

I did also look a bit at INLAjoint when trying to figure this out, but since I want this code (in my package) to generalize to other families than just survival models, I think it may be just as well to specify them myself for now (at least for the simple survival models I have had to deal with so far). On 25 Sep 2023 at 15:27 +0200, Emma Skarstein <emmaskar...@gmail.com>, wrote:
Hi! I'm attempting to formulate a survival model jointly with a measurement error + exposure model (as in Muff et. al (2015) (https://www.jstor.org/stable/24771892) and more specifically Skarstein et. al (2023), example 4.3 (https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/bimj.202300078)), but I would like to do this using inla.stacks. So it is a Weibull survival model with a measurement error model for one covariate, and that introduces two additional levels to the model. I have formulated the model successfully by specifying the matrices manually (this can be found here: https://emmaskarstein.github.io/Missing-data-and-measurement-error/missing_and_mismeasured_covariate.html#me-model-ignoring-missing-observations) So I feel like it should not be a problem using inla.stacks to structure the data instead, but I'm struggling with the structure of the survival response.

One option, following this example: https://becarioprecario.bitbucket.io/spde-gitbook/ch-risk.html, would be to specify the time and event for inla.surv as separate vectors to the stack, and then call inla.surv directly in the formula. However, since I also need to include the responses for the measurement error model and exposure model in the formula, that won't work.

The other approach, more closely following my previous implementation using the matrices directly, would involve passing the inla.surv object as one list element to the stack data, together with two columns of NAs, and naming the list of all three of these Y. Then the formula could just have Y on the left hand side. However, when passing the inla.surv-object as one of the elements in a list as the data input in inla.stack, I get the error "Error in as.data.frame.default(x[[i]], optional = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = stringsAsFactors) : cannot coerce class ‘"inla.surv"’ to a data.frame".

I noticed the documentation for inla.stack says that the data argument should be a dataframe or a list of vectors, so I'm wondering if it is at all possible to structure the data for a survival model like this using stacks?

Here is some code to illustrate the issue (I've attached the whole code that continues this example in an R-file for further context):

# Exploring survival stacks

library(INLA)

n <- 100

t <- runif(n, 0, 10) # Survival time
d <- sample(c(0,1), n, replace = TRUE) # Survival event

x <- rnorm(n, 0, 1) # Covariate with measurement error
z <- rnorm(n, 0, 1) # Covariate without measurement error

data <- data.frame(t, d, x, z)

# Regression model of interest
# eta = beta.0 + beta.x*x + beta.z*z
Y.surv <- inla.surv(data$t, data$d)

stk_moi <- inla.stack(
    data = list(Y = list(Y.surv, rep(NA, n), rep(NA, n))), # THIS FAILS
    A = list(1),
    effects = list(
      list(beta.0 = rep(1, n),
           beta.x = 1:n,
           beta.z = data$z)),
    tag = "moi")
